rationale: One localized, self-contained defect: sys_clock_getres is entirely absent from both syscall tables (x86.rs jumps 228 CLOCK_GETTIME -> 230 CLOCK_NANOSLEEP, skipping 229; generic.rs jumps 113 -> 115, skipping 114), so the test fails on an unimplemented syscall rather than on a subsystem Asterinas lacks. The fix is additive and narrow: clock_getres only reports a clock's resolution, takes no locks, and touches no filesystem or scheduling state. All the infrastructure it needs already exists -- the ClockId enum in kernel/src/syscall/clock_gettime.rs already enumerates exactly the 8 positive clock IDs the test exercises (REALTIME, MONOTONIC, PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID, THREAD_CPUTIME_ID, MONOTONIC_RAW, REALTIME_COARSE, MONOTONIC_COARSE, BOOTTIME), and read_clock already validates them plus the negative dynamic-clock encoding, so the new handler can reuse that same validation to get the EINVAL-for--1 case the test also checks. The test tolerates unimplemented clocks gracefully (it downgrades an EINVAL to TCONF), so only the resolution values and the argument validation actually have to be right, and a NULL res pointer must succeed -- two of the six variants pass NULL. Verified on the host: clock_getres01 passes on real Linux with the pinned LTP 20260529 binary, so the failure is Asterinas's, not the test's. Verified in Asterinas at base e8f2b9ca6: clock_getres01 fails while clock_gettime01 passes in the same boot, isolating the missing syscall from the working clock infrastructure underneath it. Preferred over the other measured failures because each of those is broader or murkier: brk02 needs VMA split/merge and munmap-across-VMAs behavior; open04 is an RLIMIT_NOFILE/EMFILE accounting issue; statfs03 and utimes01 both need seteuid-based permission checks (statfs03 EACCES on a search-permission-denied path prefix, utimes01 five distinct errno cases including EROFS on a read-only mount); sched_setaffinity01 and the socket tests (getsockname01, getpeername01, shutdown01/02, pipe2_*) came back broken rather than merely failing, which points at harness or setup problems that would have to be untangled before any kernel defect is even visible.
notes: Round 1 of 10, nothing named by the user, so suite and test were both auto-picked; ltp is the first suite in priority order and its all.txt pool is non-empty (976 commented entries), so it is the answer. No collision: the only other runs are ltp/fsync03 (run-7UHmXC, committed) and ltp/dup02 (run-atDPcd, committed); neither touched clock_getres01 and no run is stalled or in-progress besides this one. Cache handling: the pre-existing select.cache records all came from commit 68bdd4a99, which is NOT an ancestor of this run's base e8f2b9ca6 -- the two share merge-base 8a9543109 and are parallel branches, with 13 extra kernel commits on my side (the FsType refactor, ClosedFile, and the range-lock owner-model fix). Per cache.md that makes those probe records weak hints only, so I did not trust them and probed fresh; their host records remain valid since the pinned LTP version 20260529 is unchanged. The previous run also probed alphabetically and stopped at mknod04, leaving 711 commented candidates with a matching binary entirely unmeasured, which is the ground I covered. Measured this round and appended 96 records to select.cache: 47 host records (42 pass, 5 tconf) and 32 probe records, of which 17 are also emitted as stale-entry. Those 17 already pass in Asterinas at e8f2b9ca6 while still blocked in all.txt, and are the readiest work for later rounds -- brk01, clock_gettime01, madvise01, madvise05, pause01, pause02, personality01, personality02, sched_getscheduler02, sched_getaffinity01, statfs01, statfs02, statvfs01, statvfs02, truncate03_64, memfd_create01, memfd_create02. Ruled out without an Asterinas boot, from host behavior alone: eventfd06, getdents01, getdents02, madvise02, and select02 return TCONF on real Linux. The host tbroke results I saw for eventfd01-05, writev03, fork13, mmap22, clock_gettime02/03, sched_getscheduler01, and sched_rr_get_interval01-03 are artifacts of this container (tst_kconfig.c cannot parse a kernel .config, and one timed out under my 60s wrapper) rather than test defects, so I did not record them as host observations -- they are unresolved, not eliminated, and a later round should re-measure them properly. clock_getres01 appears only in all.txt and in no blocked pool, so the default configuration applies and run_vars is empty (no CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR override).
